mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals strong labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 4.0%, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust economic growth and consumer confidence, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through improved corporate earnings and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between GDPC1 and HOUST is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 60-day returns on the interaction term, or the combined signal fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases when both series are above their 50th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL above 2.5%) triggers a monetary tightening cycle that increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns during the tightening phase.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL is above 2.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth (over the past 3 months) and 5-day SPX returns is negative (i.e., higher payroll growth associated with lower returns) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is below 100.0, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and housing market activity, which together boost corporate revenues and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between RSAFS and HOUST is not significant (p>0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term, or the combined signal fails to produce positive returns in more than 50% of cases when both series are above their 50th percentile.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE above 5.0%) signals economic distress and reduced consumer spending, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns during recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is above 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
